meta.$comment: Klive's own description of the Boriel ZX BASIC language. Read .ai/zxbasic-syntax/README.md before editing. Arrays keyed by 'name' are kept sorted; run `node scripts/zxbasic-syntax-check.cjs` to see whether upstream changed since this was written.
meta.reading_rule: Upstream (AGPL) was read only to discover facts about the language; everything here is written independently, in Klive's own words and own EBNF. Documentation pages (CC BY 4.0, (c) Jose Rodriguez-Rosa 'Boriel' and contributors) were paraphrased with attribution.
meta.ebnf_conventions: '=' defines; '|' alternatives; '[ ]' optional; '{ }' zero or more; '( )' grouping; "x" literal token; keywords are case-insensitive; NL = end of line; SEP = end of line or ':'; block = { line }.
meta.confidence_markers: 'unverified' in a notes field means the fact was inferred from documentation or behaviour, not confirmed against the implementation.

case_sensitivity.keywords: always case-insensitive (PRINT, print, PrInT are the same token)
case_sensitivity.identifiers: case-sensitive by default; case-insensitive with --ignore-case, #pragma case_insensitive = true, or --sinclair
case_sensitivity.notes: Standard-library files switch case_insensitive on for their own scope with #pragma push(case_insensitive) ... #pragma pop(case_insensitive).

comments.notes: REM must be followed by a blank, tab or end of line. As a statement it needs a preceding ':' when it follows another statement on the line.
Needs no ':' before it. The apostrophe is never a PRINT separator in ZX BASIC.
May span lines, may sit in the middle of a statement (the statement continues after it), and nests: each /' raises a depth counter, each '/ lowers it.

line_structure.continuation: A '_' or '\' as the last token of a line (a trailing ' or REM comment may follow it) joins the next physical line. No label is recognised at the start of a continued line.
line_structure.line_numbers: Optional. A decimal integer at the start of a line (only blanks before it) is a label. A non-integer number there is an error. Line order is irrelevant; duplicate line numbers are errors.
line_structure.labels: An identifier at the start of a line (only blanks before it) followed by optional blanks and ':' declares a label. Since 1.18.0 labels are recognised only at the beginning of a line. Labels are global even when declared inside SUB/FUNCTION.
line_structure.directives: A '#' as the first non-blank character starts a preprocessor directive line. A '#' anywhere else is an illegal character.

identifiers.letters: ASCII A-Z a-z. The lexer accepts a leading underscore (documentation says names start with a letter).

sigils.notes: The sigil is stripped from the stored name, so a$ and a name the same variable. A sigil that contradicts the variable's declared or inferred type is an error (tightened in 1.19.0). '&' for Long exists in the internal table but lexes as the bAND operator, so it cannot be used (unverified).

identifiers.spelling_aliases: CHR$, STR$, INKEY$ are accepted spellings of CHR, STR, INKEY. SCREEN$ and SCREEN are accepted after SAVE/LOAD/VERIFY. A SUB/FUNCTION name may carry '$'; a $-suffixed FUNCTION must return String.
identifiers.reserved: Reserved words (see keywords) cannot be identifiers.

numeric_literals.notes: optional fraction, optional exponent e|E [+|-] digits
The h-suffix form must start with a digit (C9h is an identifier).
BIN is a keyword: the token after it is read as binary digits; BIN followed by a non-binary token yields 0. 00B is binary, 00Bh is hex.

literal_typing.integer: smallest type that holds the value: 0..255 UByte; -128..127 Byte; 0..65535 UInteger; -32768..32767 Integer; other negative Long; other positive ULong. A negative literal is unary minus on a positive literal, folded at compile time.
literal_typing.real: a non-integer literal in the open range (-32768, 32767) is Fixed; otherwise Float
literal_typing.based: binary, hex and octal literals are unsigned, sized by value

string_literals.doubled_quote: "" inside a literal is one double quote

escapes.meaning: block-graphics characters 128..143: 128 + P(x) + N(y), P: space=0 '=2 .=8 :=10, N: space=0 '=1 .=4 :=5
character with decimal code nnn (exactly three digits)
embedded INVERSE control code (chr 20, N); N in {0,1,n,i}

string_literals.notes: Any other character is taken literally. Documentation mentions \` for the pound sign; no such lexer rule was found (a plain backtick already is the pound sign in the Spectrum character set) - unverified. Multi-line literals: unverified, not recommended.

keywords.name: END
keywords.notes: also closes SUB, FUNCTION, IF, WHILE and ASM blocks

keywords.name: GO
keywords.notes: GO TO / GO SUB two-word forms

keywords_notes.directive_names: After '#': define undef include ifdef ifndef if else endif error warning line init require pragma push pop once (case-insensitive).
keywords_notes.library_names_to_avoid: Not reserved but provided by the standard library: ASC ATTR CSRLIN HEX HEX16 INPUT INPUT42 GETKEY MULTIKEYS GETKEYSCANCODE LCASE UCASE POINT POS PRINT42 PRINTAT42 PRINT64 PRINTAT64 SCREEN$ MID$ LEFT$ RIGHT$ STRPOS STRPOS2 INSTR LTRIM RTRIM TRIM ISDIGIT ISLETTER ROUND ALLOCATE.

primitives.name: Float
primitives.range: Sinclair ROM 40-bit float: 1 exponent byte (excess 128) + 4 mantissa bytes

primitives.name: String
primitives.range: pointer to a heap block: 2-byte length followed by the characters; max 65535 characters; null pointer means the empty string

types.boolean: Internal only (result of comparisons and logical operators): 1 byte, 0 or 1; cannot be named; converts to UByte in arithmetic.

categories.integral: Byte UByte Integer UInteger Long ULong (+boolean)

types.default_type: An untyped identifier takes its type from context (assigned expression, common type of FOR bounds, sigil, READ target, parameter or return position). If nothing determines it, the type is Float with warning W100. Under --strict an implicit type is an error; under --explicit every variable and function must be declared before use.
types.initial_values: Numeric variables start at zero, strings at the empty string.
types.common_type_rule: For two operands: same type -> that type; either Float -> Float; else either Fixed -> Fixed; else String with non-String -> error; else the larger size, made signed if either operand is signed (UByte+Byte -> Byte, UInteger+Byte -> Integer). An operand of unknown type takes the other's type.

conversions.numeric: implicit between numeric types (assignment, parameters, arguments, built-ins)
conversions.string: never implicit; use VAL() and STR()
conversions.constants: constant conversion to an integral type truncates toward minus infinity and masks to the target width; a value that does not fit raises W120
conversions.bitwise_on_decimals: bitwise operators on Fixed/Float operands compute in Long
conversions.whole_array_assignment: requires identical element type and identical total byte size; differing dimension shapes only warn

types.sizeof: SIZEOF(type) and SIZEOF(variable) are compile-time constants in bytes.

strings.representation: length-prefixed heap strings; assignment copies; '+' concatenates; comparisons are lexicographic
slicing: slice = str-designator "(" [ expr ] "TO" [ expr ] ")" ;   (* substring, inclusive bounds *)
str-designator = identifier | string-literal | "(" string-expr ")" | array-element | function-call ;
strings.slice_rules: Indices are relative to string_base (default 0; --string-base 1 or --sinclair make them 1-based). A missing lower bound is the first character, a missing upper bound the last. Bounds clip to 0..65534; lower > upper yields the empty string. Constant slices of constant strings fold at compile time.
strings.heap: Heap size defaults to 4768 bytes (--heap-size). A string that does not fit becomes empty unless --debug-memory, which raises the ROM 'Out of memory' report.

operators.precedence_notes: NOT a = b parses as NOT (a = b); a bAND 3 = 1 as (a bAND 3) = 1; a bAND b + 1 as a bAND (b + 1); 2^3^2 = 512; -2^2 = -(2^2). The table was carried over from the pre-1.19 LALR grammar; that the Lark grammar reproduces it exactly is unverified.

list.result: common type; unary minus converts an unsigned operand to its signed counterpart
common type; integer division when both operands are integral

list.name: SHL / <<
list.operands: integral left (Fixed/Float left converts to ULong); right converted to UByte
variable, array element with constant subscripts, or label
list.result: UInteger address; a compile-time constant for globals and labels, a run-time value for locals

operators.restrictions: Strings cannot be operands of - * / MOD AND OR XOR bAND bOR bXOR SHL SHR. Constant sub-expressions fold at compile time, including literal string concatenation and comparison. A condition that is a numeric constant raises W110.
primary_expressions: primary = number | string-literal | "PI" | identifier | identifier "(" [ args ] ")" | identifier expr | slice | "(" expr ")" | "@" address-designator | builtin-call ;
operators.primary_notes: identifier(args) is a function call, an array element or a string slice depending on what the identifier names. identifier expr is a single-argument call without parentheses. A bare identifier is a variable or a call to a parameterless FUNCTION. A SUB cannot appear in an expression. A bare array name is allowed only as a whole-array argument or in whole-array assignment.

statements.name: ASM
statements.semantics: Passes the enclosed lines verbatim to the built-in Z80 assembler. Preprocessor macros expand inside the block; #line, #init and #require may appear inside it.
statements.constraints: Global variables and routines are visible to the assembler as _name (BASIC name with the sigil stripped); user labels and line numbers as .LABEL._name; locals and parameters live on the stack and have no name; runtime symbols are in the .core namespace. Inline asm in a FASTCALL routine needs no ret. See inline_asm.

statements.name: BEEP
statements.semantics: Sounds the beeper: duration in seconds, then pitch in semitones relative to middle C. Both operands convert to Float.

statements.name: BOLD
statements.semantics: Permanent attribute statement (ZX BASIC extension): emphasised glyphs when the operand (converted to UByte) is non-zero. Also usable as a PRINT modifier.

statements.name: BORDER
statements.semantics: Sets the border colour; the operand converts to UByte.

statements.name: BRIGHT
statements.semantics: Permanent attribute statement; operand converts to UByte. Also a PRINT modifier.

statements.name: CIRCLE
statements.semantics: Draws a circle at x, y with radius r. Each of the three operands converts to Byte (signed 8-bit). Optional attribute modifiers apply to this statement only.

statements.name: CLS
statements.semantics: Clears the screen with the current permanent attributes.

statements.name: CONST
statements.semantics: Declares a compile-time constant. The value must be a constant expression (numbers, operators, @ of globals or labels) or a string literal (string constants since 1.17.1). A constant is not a variable; a string constant can be sliced.

statements.name: CONTINUE
statements.semantics: Restarts the innermost enclosing loop of the named kind (goes to its next iteration). An error when no enclosing loop of that kind exists.

statements.name: DATA
statements.semantics: Provides items for READ. Items may be numeric or string expressions, including non-constant ones, which are evaluated when READ executes. Global scope only: DATA inside a SUB/FUNCTION is an error.

statements.name: DECLARE
statements.semantics: Forward-declares a SUB or FUNCTION header without a body, so it can be called before its definition with a known signature. The later definition must match name, parameter count, types and BYREF-ness (renamed parameters warn). A DECLARE after the definition, or a second definition, is an error.

statements.name: DIM
syntax: const-address = const-expr | "@" identifier | "@" identifier "(" const-expr { "," const-expr } ")" | "@" label ;
statements.semantics: Declares scalars or arrays. Several scalars may share one DIM; the initialised (= expr) and mapped (AT) forms take one name. '= expr': a compile-time constant (not a string) becomes the static initial value, otherwise an assignment is emitted at that point; the type is inferred when AS is omitted. 'AT addr' aliases the variable to a constant address (number, @global, @label or @array(const subscripts)); inside a routine a mapped variable is static. Arrays: bounds are non-negative constants with lower <= upper; a single bound n means array_base TO n; any number of dimensions; string elements allowed; elements are contiguous row-major; @a(0) is the first element's address. '=> {...}' initialises numeric arrays; nesting depth and counts must match the bounds; string arrays cannot be initialised; => and AT cannot be combined. Inside SUB/FUNCTION, DIM allocates stack locals released on return; parameters cannot be re-DIMmed.
statements.constraints: Arrays must be declared before use. Declaring a variable that was already referenced is an error. A non-constant AT address or initialiser is an error. Array subscripts convert to UInteger.

statements.name: DO
statements.semantics: DO ... LOOP alone loops forever (the recommended infinite loop). Bottom-tested forms run the body at least once; top-tested forms test first. DO LOOP UNTIL c on one line is allowed. An empty body raises W130.

statements.name: DRAW
statements.semantics: Draws a line relative to the last plotted point: dx, dy convert to Integer; the optional third operand is an arc angle in radians (Float).

statements.name: END
statements.semantics: Ends the program and returns to the caller (BASIC or the OS) with the optional value (default 0). END also pairs with SUB, FUNCTION, IF, WHILE and ASM to close blocks.

statements.name: ERROR
statements.semantics: Raises the ROM error report with the given number (operand converts to UByte).

statements.name: EXIT
statements.semantics: Leaves the innermost enclosing loop of the named kind. An error when no enclosing loop of that kind exists.

statements.name: FLASH
statements.semantics: Permanent attribute statement; operand converts to UByte. Also a PRINT modifier.

statements.name: FOR
syntax: for = "FOR" identifier "=" expr "TO" expr [ "STEP" expr ] SEP block "NEXT" [ identifier ] ;
statements.semantics: Counted loop; STEP defaults to 1. NEXT may name the loop variable, and if it does it must match. An undeclared loop variable takes the common type of the three expressions (FOR i = 1 TO 10 gives UByte; FOR i = -1 TO 10 gives Byte), so wrap-around of that type can make a loop endless. Constant analysis warns for STEP 0 and for ranges that never iterate.

statements.name: FUNCTION
syntax: function-def = "FUNCTION" [ convention ] identifier [ "(" [ params ] ")" ] [ "AS" type ] NL body "END" "FUNCTION" ;
param = [ "BYVAL" | "BYREF" ] identifier [ "AS" type ] [ "=" const-expr ] | [ "BYREF" ] identifier "(" ")" "AS" type ;
statements.semantics: Defines a value-returning routine; RETURN expr returns the value (converted to the return type). An untyped return defaults to Float (W100; error under --strict). Falling off the end raises W190. See subprograms for parameter passing, calling conventions and calls.

statements.name: GO
statements.semantics: Two-word spellings of GOTO and GOSUB.

statements.name: GOSUB
statements.semantics: Calls the code at a label or line number; RETURN at global scope comes back. Not allowed inside SUB/FUNCTION. Targets may be used before they are declared; an undeclared target is an error at the end of parsing.

statements.name: GOTO
statements.semantics: Jumps to a label or line number. Labels are global; jumping into a SUB/FUNCTION is not possible.

statements.name: IF
syntax: if-block = "IF" expr [ "THEN" ] NL block { "ELSEIF" expr [ "THEN" ] [ NL ] block } [ "ELSE" [ NL ] block ] ( "END" "IF" | "ENDIF" ) ;
statements.semantics: THEN is optional. The single-line form keeps everything on one line. ELSE IF written as two words is a nested IF that needs its own END IF. Labels may precede body lines. An empty IF is dropped with W140.

statements.name: INK
statements.semantics: Permanent attribute statement; operand converts to UByte. Also a PRINT modifier.

statements.name: INVERSE
statements.semantics: Permanent attribute statement; operand converts to UByte. Also a PRINT modifier.

statements.name: ITALIC
statements.semantics: Permanent attribute statement (ZX BASIC extension): slanted glyphs when non-zero. Also a PRINT modifier.

statements.name: LET
syntax: substr-assignment = [ "LET" ] string-array "(" args ")" "(" [ expr ] "TO" [ expr ] ")" "=" string-expr ;
statements.semantics: LET is optional everywhere. The right side converts to the variable's type. Substring assignment overwrites characters in place; for a string array element one extra subscript is the character index. There are no compound assignment operators.
statements.constraints: Assigning to a constant, function or label is an error; assigning an array to a scalar is an error; whole-array copy needs identical element type and total size.

statements.name: LOAD
statements.semantics: Loads from tape: CODE with optional address and length; SCREEN$ is CODE 16384, 6912; DATA loads the bytes of one scalar or whole array, or without a name the whole user-variable area plus heap. Load errors do not stop the program (check PEEK 23610); BREAK cancels.

statements.name: ON
statements.semantics: Computed jump through a jump table: the expression converts to UByte; value 0 selects the first target; out-of-range values do nothing.

statements.name: OUT
statements.semantics: Writes a byte to an I/O port: port converts to UInteger, value to UByte.

statements.name: OVER
statements.semantics: Permanent attribute statement; operand converts to UByte. Also a PRINT modifier.

statements.name: PAPER
statements.semantics: Permanent attribute statement; operand converts to UByte. Also a PRINT modifier.

statements.name: PAUSE
statements.semantics: Waits the given number of frames (operand converts to UInteger); 0 waits for a key press (or 65536 frames).

statements.name: PLOT
statements.semantics: Plots a pixel at x, y (both convert to UByte); (0,0) is bottom-left and all 192 rows are usable. Optional attribute modifiers apply to this statement only.

statements.name: POKE
statements.semantics: Writes to memory. Without a type: address converts to UInteger, value to UByte. With a type the value is converted to and stored as that type (POKE UINTEGER 23675, v; POKE FLOAT a, PI). The comma-after-type form is accepted for FreeBASIC compatibility.

statements.name: PRINT
syntax: print-item = expr | "AT" expr "," expr | "TAB" expr | attr-modifier ;
statements.semantics: ';' juxtaposes, ',' advances to the next 16-column field, a trailing separator suppresses the newline, a bare PRINT outputs a newline. AT row, col (both UByte; all 24 rows usable); TAB col (UByte, taken modulo 32, moves to the next line when already past the column). Attribute modifiers inside PRINT are temporary for that statement. Boolean expressions print as 0 or 1. The apostrophe is not a separator.

statements.name: RANDOMIZE
statements.semantics: Seeds the random generator with the operand (converted to ULong); without an operand it seeds from the FRAMES counter.

statements.name: READ
statements.semantics: Reads the next DATA items into scalars or array elements (a whole array is an error). An undeclared target becomes Float. Reading past the last item wraps to the first.

statements.name: RESTORE
statements.semantics: Makes the next READ start at the first DATA item, or at the DATA line following the given label or line number.

statements.name: RETURN
statements.semantics: At global scope returns from GOSUB. Inside a SUB returns. Inside a FUNCTION it must carry a value of the function's category (numeric vs string), which converts to the return type. RETURN expr outside a FUNCTION is an error.

statements.name: SAVE
statements.semantics: Saves to tape: CODE address, length; SCREEN$ is CODE 16384, 6912; DATA saves one scalar or whole array, or without a name the whole user-variable area plus heap.

statements.name: STOP
statements.semantics: Raises a ROM report; without an operand the 'STOP statement' report.

statements.name: SUB
syntax: sub-def = "SUB" [ convention ] identifier [ "(" [ params ] ")" ] NL body "END" "SUB" ;
statements.semantics: Defines a routine without a return value; a SUB cannot declare a return type and cannot be used in an expression. See subprograms for parameters, conventions and calls.

statements.name: VERIFY
statements.semantics: Same forms as LOAD; compares the tape block with memory instead of loading it.

statements.name: WHILE
statements.semantics: Top-tested loop. An empty body raises W130.

statements_notes.labels_and_addresses: label: and line numbers declare global labels of pointer type; @label is a compile-time constant address, used with USR @label, DIM x AT @label, POKE, RESTORE label and array initialisers. @global is constant; @local is a run-time value; a bare @array yields the array's data label (1.18.3).
statements_notes.prologue: Unless --headerless: the program prologue disables interrupts, saves IX, IY and HL', stores SP, re-enables interrupts, calls every #init routine and jumps to the main code; the epilogue restores them and returns to BASIC. END and STOP return a code. --enable-break inserts a BREAK check per line.

functions.name: ABS
functions.notes: warns as redundant on an unsigned argument

functions.name: CHR
functions.result: String with one character per argument; parentheses mandatory

functions.name: CODE
functions.result: UByte code of the first character; 0 for the empty string

functions.name: INKEY
functions.result: String: the key currently pressed, or the empty string

functions.name: LBOUND
functions.result: UInteger lower bound; dimension omitted or 0 gives the number of dimensions; constant-folded for declared arrays

functions.name: LEN
functions.result: UInteger length; constant-folded for literals. LEN of an array gives its number of dimensions (edge case).

functions.name: PEEK
functions.result: UByte, or the named type when one is given

functions.name: SGN
functions.result: Byte: -1, 0 or 1; warns on an unsigned argument

functions.name: UBOUND
functions.result: UInteger upper bound; dimension omitted or 0 gives the number of dimensions; constant-folded for declared arrays

functions.name: USR
functions.argument: address converted to UInteger, or a string
functions.result: UInteger: calls machine code at the address and returns BC; for a string, the UDG address of its first character (case-insensitive)

functions.name: VAL
functions.result: Float; constant strings fold at compile time (invalid gives 0 with a warning); at run time an invalid string sets the ROM error variable

functions_notes.library: Provided by #include, not built in: ATTR (attr.bas), SCREEN$ (screen.bas), POINT (point.bas), INPUT and INPUT42 (String; input.bas), POS, CSRLIN, ASC, HEX, HEX16, ROUND, and from string.bas MID$, LEFT$, RIGHT$, STRPOS, STRPOS2, INSTR, UCASE/UCASE2, LCASE/LCASE2, LTRIM/RTRIM/TRIM, ISDIGIT, ISLETTER. With --sinclair the file sinclair.bas is included automatically (attr, point, screen, input, alloc; it also relocates the UDG system variable to allocated heap).

call: call = identifier | identifier "(" [ args ] ")" | identifier args ;   (* statement: SUB or FUNCTION call; the parenthesis-less form allows e.g. test x := 1 *)

parameters.default_passing: scalars BYVAL unless #pragma default_byref = true; arrays always BYREF (BYVAL on an array is an error)
parameters.byref_arguments: a BYREF argument must be a variable, an array or an array element, not an expression
parameters.optional: a parameter with '= const' is optional; a mandatory parameter after an optional one is an error; array parameters cannot have defaults
parameters.named_arguments: name := expr; positional arguments may not follow a named one; unknown names, too many or too few arguments are errors
parameters.typing: untyped parameters and returns default to Float (W100; error under --strict)

conventions.STDCALL: Default. Parameters are pushed on the stack in reverse order (last argument first); an 8-bit value occupies a word with the value in the high byte; 32-bit values are pushed high word then low word; a Float takes 6 bytes (a padding byte, then exponent, then the 4 mantissa bytes). The callee removes them. Results: A for 8-bit, HL for 16-bit and String pointers, DE:HL for 32-bit and Fixed, and for Float the register image A (exponent), E, D, C, B (mantissa, sign in bit 7 of E). The docs pages fastcall.md/stdcall.md describe the Float result as C/DE/HL; the implementation and runtime use A/E/D/C/B (verified against the backend and runtime headers).
conventions.FASTCALL: The first parameter arrives in registers according to its size: A (8-bit), HL (16-bit or String pointer), DE:HL (32-bit or Fixed), A/E/D/C/B (Float). No stack frame is set up and locals are not allowed. Results as for STDCALL. More than one parameter raises W160; the remaining ones are pushed STDCALL-style ([SP+0] return address, [SP+2] second parameter, ...) and the routine must remove them itself.

subprograms.rules: Recursion is allowed. Locals are DIMmed inside the body. DATA and GOSUB are not allowed inside routines. A FUNCTION called before its definition is checked at the end of parsing; without DECLARE its return type is assumed Float. Unused routines are removed at -O1 and above (W170).

preprocessor.overview: Runs before parsing (and again over the generated assembly in asm output mode). A directive line starts with '#' as its first non-blank character; blanks may follow '#'; names are case-insensitive.

directives.name: #define
directives.semantics: Object-like or function-like macro. The parameter list must follow the name without a space. The body may continue over lines ending in '\' or '_'. Duplicate parameter names are errors; redefinition raises W510 (W500 for a built-in); no whitespace after the name raises W520. Expansion is lazy and recursive; arguments may contain nested parentheses and commas inside them; the argument count must match. '##' pastes tokens, '#' stringizes (the result is a BASIC string with doubled quotes).

directives.name: #error
directives.semantics: Emits a compile error with the text.

directives.name: #if
directives.semantics: Conditional compilation. pp-expr uses macro names, integers, strings, parentheses, ==, != or <>, <, <=, >, >=, && and ||. Equality compares expanded text; ordering compares integer values (non-numeric counts as 0); a bare name is true when it expands to a non-zero integer or, failing that, when it is defined. Whether #elif is implemented is unverified.

directives.name: #ifndef
directives.semantics: True when NAME is not defined.

directives.name: #include
directives.semantics: <file> searches the include path: the architecture's stdlib/, runtime/, then -I directories (zx81sd falls back to zx48k). "file" tries the current file's directory first. Absolute paths are allowed. A MACRO must expand to one of the two forms (1.15.1). Recursive inclusion warns. 'once' includes only if not already included (a later inclusion is silently empty; a warning when included from several places). The [arch:zx48k] modifier looks the file up in another architecture's library; any modifier name other than arch is an error.

directives.name: #init
directives.semantics: Registers an assembler routine (dotted names allowed) to be called in the program prologue. Used inside ASM blocks of libraries.

directives.name: #line
directives.semantics: Resets line and file bookkeeping for diagnostics.

directives.name: #pragma
directives.semantics: Sets, saves or restores a compiler option (see pragmas). Values are integers, identifiers or strings; booleans accept true/false, on/off, yes/no, +/-. An unknown option raises W300. 'once' marks the current file as include-once.

directives.name: #require
directives.semantics: Requests a runtime assembler module to be appended to the output (an include-once of that file).

directives.name: #warning
directives.semantics: Emits a compile warning with the text.

builtin_macros.notes: -D NAME[=VALUE] defines further macros. The runtime honours -D HIDE_LOAD_MSG to hide LOAD messages.

pragmas.name: explicit
pragmas.effect: variables must be declared before use

pragmas.name: force_asm_brackets
pragmas.effect: as the CLI flag of the same name (assembler bracket style)

pragmas.name: heap_address
pragmas.effect: fixed heap address instead of after the program

pragmas.name: once
pragmas.effect: marks the current file as include-once

pragmas.name: string_base
pragmas.effect: index of the first character of a string

pragmas.name: zxnext
pragmas.effect: ZX Next opcodes allowed in ASM blocks

preprocessor.pragmas_notes: Any compiler option can be set through #pragma; the ones above are the meaningful ones. push/pop save and restore a single option, which the standard library uses around its own case_insensitive setting.

inline_asm.delimiters: ASM on a line of its own ... END ASM on a line of its own; ';' starts an assembler comment
inline_asm.upstream_dialect: The built-in assembler (zxbasm) accepts DEFB/DEFW/DEFS, ALIGN n, PROC/LOCAL/ENDP local label scopes, #incbin, temporary labels 1b/1f, and namespaces (the compiler uses .core, .LABEL and .DATA). Curly braces are tolerated for third-party assembler compatibility. Z80N opcodes need --zxnext or --arch zxnext. Preprocessor macros expand inside the block.
inline_asm.symbol_visibility: Global variables and routines: _name (sigil stripped). Labels and line numbers: .LABEL._name (for example .LABEL._10). Locals and parameters: stack (IX-relative), no name. Runtime: .core namespace. The usual BASIC-side idiom is @label / @var for addresses and USR @label to call code; a label line immediately before an ASM block is the documented way to address data inside it. That _name is exactly what the assembler sees for every global is unverified.
inline_asm.klive_rule: Klive's compiler accepts inline asm in Klive's native assembler dialect (decision recorded 2026-09-26). How BASIC symbols are exposed to it is defined by the compiler plan, not by upstream.

diagnostics.uncoded_warnings: useless FOR ranges, STEP 0, arrays with different dimension shapes in a copy, SGN or ABS of an unsigned value, parameters renamed relative to a DECLARE, deprecated CLI flags
diagnostics.errors: Errors carry no numeric codes. Main classes: undeclared identifier, array or label; identifier used with the wrong class (variable, array, function, sub, label); duplicate declaration (variable, constant, label, line number, function, parameter); array used before declaration; array bounds not constant, negative or reversed; AT address or initialiser not constant; initialiser shape mismatch; string array initialiser; string/number conversion required (use VAL or STR); operator applied to strings; wrong expression type; FOR/NEXT variable mismatch; unclosed loop or block; EXIT/CONTINUE outside such a loop; GOSUB inside a routine; RETURN with a value outside FUNCTION, SUB returning a value, FUNCTION returning nothing, wrong return category; DECLARE/definition mismatch; declared but never implemented; wrong argument count, unknown or misordered named argument; BYREF needs a variable; array passed by value; mandatory parameter after an optional one; DATA inside a routine; READ of a whole array; non-integer line number; sigil contradicting the variable type; unexpected token, end of line or end of file; preprocessor: file not found, invalid directive or filename, macro argument count mismatch, duplicated macro parameter.

codebank.origin: NextBuild Studio's fork zxbasic 1.18.7-nb10 (em00k/NextBuildStudio, bare-bones-files/NextBuildv10/zxbasic1.18.7-nb10), AGPL-derived. Only the syntax and the observable contract are recorded here; Klive implements it independently.
codebank.status: not upstream; upstream 1.19.0 has no banked-code syntax
syntax: codebank-block = "CODEBANK" const-expr NL { routine-def | dim-stmt | asm-block | label-decl } "END" "CODEBANK" ;   (* not allowed inside a SUB/FUNCTION *)
codebank-pragma = "#pragma" "codebank" "=" const-expr ;   (* bank 0 = resident; reset with #pragma codebank = 0 after an #include *)
farptr = "FARPTR" identifier ;   (* ULong: bank in bits 16..23, address in bits 0..15; for an array, the data address *)
asm-pseudo-op = "CODEBANK" const-expr ;   (* inside ASM: switch the bank of following asm lines *)
codebank.farmem_api: #include <farmem.bas>: FarPeek(p), FarPeekW(p), FarPoke(p, v), FarPokeW(p, v), FarCopy(dst, src, len), FarCopyTo(dst, src, len), FarStr(p) - each takes FARPTR values (ULong)
codebank.semantics: SUB and FUNCTION bodies inside a bank are compiled into an 8K page that is paged into a code window (default $6000-$7FFF, MMU slot 3 via NextReg $53; a 16K window is optional). Call sites are unchanged: each banked routine keeps a 6-byte resident trampoline (call far-call helper, bank byte, body address) that pages the bank in, keeps a 3-byte-per-level shadow stack and redirects the return through a far-return helper, so stack frames and argument offsets are unchanged. Same-bank calls take a fast path. Bank-local data: DIMs inside the block, module-level asm and labels, INCBIN; reachable from outside only through FARPTR and the farmem API. Resident: ordinary statements, the runtime, string literals, DATA, the heap, non-bank globals.

errors: a bank larger than the window
direct GOTO, jp or call between different banks
references into a bank from outside it
an asm block that does not return to its starting segment

warnings.W910: a bank holds data but no routine
warnings.W920: bare @array used in a bank context

unchecked: interrupt routines must not make far calls or remap the window
SP must never point into the window

cli.name: --code-bank-depth
cli.meaning: far-call nesting depth (3 bytes per level)

codebank.outputs: <name>.bank<N>.bin per non-empty bank; <name>.banks.json manifest {window, window_size, banks: [{bank, file, org, size, page, pages}]}; banked labels carry a B<n>: prefix in the .map file. The NextBuild build turns the manifest into NEX page loads and checks page overlaps with packed data.

syntax_relevant: parser ported to Lark (no intended syntax change; the grammar is now embedded in generated form)
a sigil that contradicts the variable's type is now an error (previously accepted)
new docs pages bin.md (BIN literal prefix) and tab.md (PRINT TAB)
new Play library (AY/Next sound) and maskedsprites library merged (library, not language)
labels are recognised only at the beginning of a line
boolean values normalised: comparisons and logical operators always yield 0 or 1; --strict-bool deprecated
changes.notes: 1.18.1-1.18.7 were bug-fix releases with no syntax change (i32/u32 casts, ByRef with array elements, @array label emission, Fixed to Long conversion, decimal casts truncating toward minus infinity, zxnext backend fixes). Library additions: hmirror.bas (1.18.2), getPaintData/getChars in putchars.bas (1.18.3), scroll-aligned functions (1.18.4). The date is approximate (unverified).

docs_errata.$comment: Places where upstream docs pages disagree with each other or with the implementation. The spec follows the implementation; these notes stop a future session from 'correcting' the spec back to the docs.
items: fastcall.md and stdcall.md give the Float result registers as C/DE/HL; the backend and runtime use A (exponent) plus E/D/C/B (mantissa). The spec follows the implementation.
zxb.md: the option help says the default optimisation level is 2, the prose says 1. The implementation default is 2.
zxb.md: the prose calls -e "--stderr"; the option is --errmsg. The prose uses zxb.py, the help uses zxbc.py (zxb is the historical name).
operators.md documents precedence only for ^, * / MOD and + -. The full table in operators.precedence comes from the implementation.
types.md marks ULong as signed (typo) and does not state the width of the % sigil (16-bit Integer).
print.md never documents ',' as a PRINT separator although examples use it; ',' advances to the next 16-column field.
paper.md says the value range is 1-8 but lists 0-8; ink.md says INK 9 is not supported.
return.md mentions a --stack-check option that is not in the option list and not implemented in 1.19.0.
rnd.md's example uses FreeBASIC-style 'As Double' and 'Function = ...', neither of which is ZX BASIC syntax.
Pages linked but missing from the docs set: memory_heap.md, zxbasm.md, pragma.md, zxbpp.md, addroperator.md, scope.md, len.md.

semantics.$comment: The semantics annex (plan R8): one entry per behaviour question the syntax does not answer. status: 'decided' (settled), 'provisional' (implemented and tested, to be confirmed against the zxbc oracle, D12), or 'open' (to settle by the given phase). source: 'docs' (upstream documentation), 'oracle' (observed zxbc behaviour) or 'klive-decision'. Every decided or provisional entry names the test that pins it.

entries.name: argument-evaluation-order
entries.question: In which order are a call's arguments evaluated, and a binary operator's operands? (Observable when they call FUNCTIONs with side effects.)
entries.decision: A call's arguments last first, so the stack machine leaves them where STDCALL wants them; a binary operator's left operand before its right. Awaits the oracle.

entries.name: constant-arithmetic-literal
entries.question: What type does arithmetic on number literals alone have?
entries.decision: Literal-only arithmetic stays exact and takes the smallest type that holds the result: 200 + 100 is 300, a UInteger; 1 - 2 is -1, a Byte.

entries.name: constant-arithmetic-typed
entries.question: Does constant arithmetic on typed values wrap to the type's width?
entries.decision: Yes: folding computes what the program would, so a typed operand (a DIMmed constant, a CAST) wraps in its type; 200 in a UByte plus 100 is 44.

entries.name: constant-integer-division-by-zero
entries.question: What does a constant integer division or MOD by zero fold to?
entries.decision: The runtime's result (every bit set; MOD gives the dividend), with warning K406. A Float or Fixed constant division by zero is error E425.

entries.name: constant-power
entries.question: How is a constant x ^ y folded?
entries.decision: As the exact power rounded to the nearest Float. The ROM computes EXP(y * LN x), which can differ in the last bit.

entries.name: elif-directive
entries.question: Is #elif accepted by the preprocessor?
entries.decision: Yes.

entries.name: for-loop-evaluation
entries.question: Are FOR's limit and step evaluated once or on every iteration, what is the variable after the loop, and how do negative and zero STEP behave?

entries.name: forward-function-call
entries.question: What signature does a FUNCTION called before its definition have when there is no DECLARE?
entries.decision: Its definition's signature: routine headers are collected before binding. Upstream assumes a Float return until the definition; Klive accepts every program upstream accepts here, and a few it rejects.

entries.name: implicit-type-from-context
entries.question: Does a variable typed by its first assignment, FOR values or READ raise W100?
entries.decision: No: W100 is raised only when nothing determines the type and it becomes Float. Under strict typing any undeclared variable is error E426.

entries.name: implicit-variable-in-routine
entries.question: Is an undeclared variable used inside a SUB or FUNCTION local or global?
entries.decision: Global when a global of that name exists at that point; otherwise local to the routine.

entries.name: integer-division-by-zero
entries.question: What does integer division or MOD by zero give at run time?
entries.decision: A quotient with every bit set; MOD gives the dividend.

entries.name: keyword-macro-names
entries.question: May a #define use a keyword as its name?
entries.decision: Yes.

entries.name: literal-integer-type
entries.question: What type does an integer literal have?
entries.decision: The smallest type that holds it, unsigned when it is not negative (0..255 UByte, 256..65535 UInteger, -128..-1 Byte, ...); Float beyond 32 bits. This gives the spec's FOR examples: FOR i = 1 TO 10 counts in UByte, FOR i = -1 TO 10 in Byte.

entries.name: logical-operators-short-circuit
entries.question: Do AND and OR skip their right operand when the left one decides the result?
entries.decision: No: both operands are always evaluated, the left first. Awaits the oracle.

entries.name: mod-sign
entries.question: Which sign does the remainder of MOD take?
entries.decision: The dividend's (the quotient truncates towards zero), in folding and at run time.

entries.name: on-goto-out-of-range
entries.question: What does ON ... GOTO/GOSUB do with a value outside its target list?
entries.decision: Nothing: execution continues after the statement.

entries.name: operator-precedence
entries.question: Does the 1.19 parser keep the precedence table recorded in operators.precedence?
entries.decision: Klive implements the recorded table.

entries.name: print-position
entries.question: Where does PRINT start, and does it prompt 'scroll?'?
entries.decision: It starts at BASIC's print position (S_POSN) and scrolls all 24 rows without a prompt.

entries.name: print-udg-codes
entries.question: What do character codes 165-255 print?
entries.decision: The UDG area's glyphs.

entries.name: read-past-end
entries.question: What does READ do after the last DATA item?
entries.decision: It wraps to the first item.

entries.name: shr-signed
entries.question: Is SHR on a signed type arithmetic or logical?
entries.decision: Arithmetic (the sign is kept) for signed types, logical for unsigned ones.

entries.name: string-concatenation-overflow
entries.question: What does a concatenation longer than 65535 characters give?
entries.decision: The empty String.

entries.name: string-escape-unknown
entries.question: What does an unknown backslash escape in a string literal give?
entries.decision: The backslash and the character, as written.

entries.name: truncation-warning-w200
entries.question: Which conversions raise W200 ('a value will be truncated')?
entries.decision: A Fixed or Float value that is not a constant, converted to an integral type by an assignment, an argument, a RETURN or a POKE.

entries.name: unused-warning-w150
entries.question: When is a variable 'never used' (W150)?
entries.decision: When it is never mentioned after its declaration: no read, no assignment, no address taken; mapped variables and BYREF parameters are exempt. Reported, like W170, only at optimisation levels above 0.

entries.name: val-constant-invalid
entries.question: What does VAL of a constant string that is not a number give?
entries.decision: 0, with warning K407.
